teams.name: Arsenal
teams.drivers: Kroenke ownership, heavy commercialization, years of fan protest over financial extraction.

teams.name: Aston Villa
teams.drivers: Genuine underdog pedigree, the 1982 European Cup win as a mid-table English club, respected Holte End history. Docked for NSWE's private-equity-funded push back into Europe, a real but smaller-scale version of the financial-doping problem.

teams.name: Bournemouth
teams.drivers: Small coastal club with a modest footprint, though recent investment is nudging it toward the modern financial game.

teams.name: Brentford
teams.drivers: Fan-turned-owner model under Benham, community-rooted West London identity survived the move to a new ground.

teams.name: Brighton
teams.drivers: Well-run, community-founded club, but its data-driven "Moneyball" identity trades raw ultra culture for boardroom cleverness.

teams.name: Chelsea
teams.drivers: Boehly/Clearlake financial engineering, multi-club loan-army strategy over organic development.

teams.name: Coventry City
teams.drivers: Fought back from ownership chaos and a decade in the wilderness, genuine Midlands industrial community.

teams.name: Crystal Palace
teams.drivers: Holmesdale Fanatics, one of the country's genuine ultra movements, real South London community identity.

teams.name: Everton
teams.drivers: People's Club identity and Goodison history are real, but hit hard by two separate Premier League points deductions in 2023-24 for breaching financial sustainability rules, plus the Friedkin Group's multi-club overlap with Roma, the same structural red flag Chelsea gets dinged for.

teams.name: Fulham
teams.drivers: Historic Craven Cottage, but American ownership under Khan pulls it toward the commercial model.

teams.name: Hull City
teams.drivers: East Yorkshire port-city working-class roots, romantic return after a 10-year absence.

teams.name: Ipswich Town
teams.drivers: East Anglian farming-community roots, modest scale, no corporate overreach.

teams.name: Leeds United
teams.drivers: Fierce Elland Road atmosphere, working-class Yorkshire identity.

teams.name: Liverpool
teams.drivers: Your club. Kop culture, YNWA, working-class Anfield roots.

teams.name: Manchester City
teams.drivers: Abu Dhabi state ownership, the same sportswashing category as PSG on your UCL table.

teams.name: Manchester United
teams.drivers: Glazer leveraged buyout, arguably English football's most despised ownership model.

teams.name: Newcastle United
teams.drivers: Genuinely passionate Geordie support undercut hard by Saudi PIF state ownership, the same sportswashing problem that sinks Man City.

teams.name: Nottingham Forest
teams.drivers: Two European Cups under Clough as the ultimate underdog story, City Ground atmosphere, East Midlands working-class base.

teams.name: Sunderland
teams.drivers: Wearside shipbuilding and mining roots, passionate Stadium of Light support, no troubling ownership issues.

teams.name: Tottenham Hotspur
teams.drivers: Historic North London identity diluted by the corporate, NFL-sharing stadium model.

teams.name: AEK Athens
teams.drivers: Founded by Greek refugees fleeing Asia Minor in the 1920s.

teams.name: Arsenal
teams.drivers: Big Six status, some old Highbury romance survives.

teams.name: Aston Villa
teams.drivers: Real history, already weighed and set aside once in favor of Liverpool.

teams.name: Atlético Madrid
teams.drivers: Cholismo had real teeth once, trophies and a new stadium pulled it mainstream.

teams.name: Barcelona
teams.drivers: Catalan identity cuts one way, financial chaos and superclub status cut the other.

teams.name: Bayern Munich
teams.drivers: Member-owned on paper, financially dominates its own league.

teams.name: Bodø/Glimt
teams.drivers: Arctic Circle romanticism, pure underdog model against Europe's giants.

teams.name: Borussia Dortmund
teams.drivers: Your club. Yellow Wall, 50+1 fan ownership.

teams.name: Club Brugge
teams.drivers: Belgium's most decorated club, loyal but not especially rebellious.

teams.name: Como
teams.drivers: Private-equity rebuild, glossy and thin on authentic identity.

teams.name: Fenerbahçe
teams.drivers: Massive Istanbul support, closer to Turkish football's establishment tier.

teams.name: Feyenoord
teams.drivers: Rotterdam's working-class answer to Ajax's polish.

teams.name: Galatasaray
teams.drivers: Welcome to Hell reputation, among the loudest atmospheres in the sport.

teams.name: Inter Milan
teams.drivers: Steady, no rebel identity, private-equity owned.

teams.name: LASK
teams.drivers: Linz regional identity, modest scale.

teams.name: Lens
teams.drivers: Bollaert-Delelis, genuine mining-town roots, family-centric fanbase.

teams.name: Lille
teams.drivers: Northern French industrial identity, working-class support.

teams.name: Liverpool
teams.drivers: Your club. Kop culture, working-class Northwest England roots.

teams.name: Manchester City
teams.drivers: State-owned, close to the opposite of everything on your list.

teams.name: Manchester United
teams.drivers: Big money, glamour-driven, closer to the establishment.

teams.name: Napoli
teams.drivers: Unmatched working-class Southern Italian passion at the Maradona. No longer your club, still genuine on its own merits.

teams.name: PSV Eindhoven
teams.drivers: Corporate Philips roots, loyal regional base anyway.

teams.name: Paris Saint-Germain
teams.drivers: Qatari state money, the sport's clearest financial-doping case.

teams.name: Porto
teams.drivers: Beats Lisbon's money through grit and organization, real tie to your Portuguese heritage.

teams.name: RB Leipzig
teams.drivers: A marketing department wearing a football club's colors.

teams.name: Real Betis
teams.drivers: Beticismo as a way of life, eternal underdog to crosstown Sevilla.

teams.name: Real Madrid
teams.drivers: Football's ultimate establishment power.

teams.name: Roma
teams.drivers: Curva Sud culture, long history as underdog to Juventus and Milan's money.

teams.name: Sabah
teams.drivers: Newer club, limited organic history yet.

teams.name: Shakhtar Donetsk
teams.drivers: Displaced from Donetsk since 2014, still fielding "home" games hundreds of miles away.

teams.name: Slavia Prague
teams.drivers: Held its identity through decades of political suppression.

teams.name: Slovan Bratislava
teams.drivers: Slovakia's most storied club, strong domestic following.

teams.name: Sporting CP
teams.drivers: Passionate Lisbon fanbase, tie to your Portuguese heritage.

teams.name: VfB Stuttgart
teams.drivers: Member-owned under Germany's 50+1 model.

teams.name: Viking
teams.drivers: Grassroots Scandinavian community football roots.

teams.name: Villarreal
teams.drivers: Small-city club that's stayed itself.

teams.name: Atlanta United
teams.drivers: Massive crowds and real drum culture, but housed in the corporate Mercedes-Benz Stadium as an NFL tenant.

teams.name: Austin FC
teams.drivers: La Murga de Austin brass band section, high-energy Q2 Stadium.

teams.name: CF Montréal
teams.drivers: 1993 NASL/USL heritage, Ultras Montréal actively resisting corporate rebrand pressure.

teams.name: Charlotte FC
teams.drivers: Banking-capital corporate franchise, turf pitch in a massive NFL stadium, synthetic origin story.

teams.name: Chicago Fire FC
teams.drivers: A genuinely traditional 1998 club, badly damaged by rebrands and corporate mismanagement, playing in Soldier Field.

teams.name: Colorado Rapids
teams.drivers: Original 1996 founder, but weak matchday terrace energy and a stadium location that hurts atmosphere.

teams.name: Columbus Crew
teams.drivers: Original 1996 founder. The Save the Crew movement, fans organizing and beating a corporate relocation attempt, is one of the strongest grassroots wins in American soccer.

teams.name: D.C. United
teams.drivers: Original 1996 founder, Barra Brava and Screaming Eagles, born at legendary RFK Stadium.

teams.name: FC Cincinnati
teams.drivers: Grassroots rise from USL, The Bailey supporter wall, deep Midwestern working-class identity.

teams.name: FC Dallas
teams.drivers: Original 1996 club (Dallas Burn), strong academy pedigree, but a suburban Frisco stadium limits real urban terrace culture.

teams.name: Houston Dynamo FC
teams.drivers: Working-class energy-city identity undercut by a fairly sterile corporate seating bowl.

teams.name: Inter Miami CF
teams.drivers: Glamour celebrity-franchise model, built on star-chasing and commercial hype over local supporter roots.

teams.name: LA Galaxy
teams.drivers: Original 1996 flagship with real history, but leaned hard into Hollywood star-chasing over grassroots culture.

teams.name: Los Angeles Football Club
teams.drivers: The 3252 is a genuinely strong ultra section, offset by a sleek, Hollywood-adjacent corporate rebrand.

teams.name: Minnesota United FC
teams.drivers: Grassroots NASL/USL heritage, the Wonderwall tradition, authentic upper Midwest identity.

teams.name: Nashville SC
teams.drivers: USL expansion roots and real Music City community energy, played in a large corporate venue.

teams.name: New England Revolution
teams.drivers: Original 1996 club, but a secondary tenant in the sterile, Kraft-owned Gillette Stadium.

teams.name: New York City Football Club
teams.drivers: Subsidiary of the Abu Dhabi-owned City Football Group, the same state-ownership category as Man City and Newcastle.

teams.name: Orlando City
teams.drivers: Organic USL expansion roots, The Wall supporter section.

teams.name: Philadelphia Union
teams.drivers: Sons of Ben literally willed this club into existence before it had a roster. Blue-collar Pennsylvania roots.

teams.name: Portland Timbers
teams.drivers: Your club. Timbers Army, Providence Park, log-slabbing tradition, 1975 NASL heritage.

teams.name: Real Salt Lake
teams.drivers: Tight-knit, authentic Rocky Mountain community identity.

teams.name: Red Bull New York
teams.drivers: Rebranded from the historic MetroStars into a corporate energy-drink marketing vehicle, the same category as RB Leipzig.

teams.name: San Diego FC
teams.drivers: Newest expansion side, hasn't had time to build organic supporter culture yet.

teams.name: San Jose Earthquakes
teams.drivers: 1974 NASL heritage is real, but ownership under John Fisher, the same owner who gutted the A's and moved them to Las Vegas, is a genuine values problem, not a rivalry one.

teams.name: Seattle Sounders FC
teams.drivers: 1974 NASL roots, March to the Match, one of the largest and most legitimately organic supporter bases in MLS. No penalty for rivalry with your clubs.

teams.name: Sporting Kansas City
teams.drivers: Original 1996 club (Wizards) with a great stadium, but a heavily sanitized, corporate matchday feel.

teams.name: St. Louis CITY SC
teams.drivers: America's First Soccer Capital roots, community-built supporter section at CITYPARK.

teams.name: Toronto FC
teams.drivers: Pioneered modern MLS supporter sections in 2007, but MLSE's corporate ownership has gentrified the identity since.

teams.name: Vancouver Whitecaps FC
teams.drivers: 1974 NASL heritage, Southsiders, organic Pacific Northwest culture. No penalty for rivalry with your clubs.

teams.name: 1. FC Köln
teams.drivers: Enormous, passionate, unmistakably working-class Rhineland support; a yo-yo club whose fans show up in the second division just the same.

teams.name: Bayer Leverkusen
teams.drivers: A literal "Werksclub," owned outright by the Bayer pharmaceutical company under a 50+1 exemption. Financial doping by another name.

teams.name: Bayern Munich
teams.drivers: Technically member-owned, but its financial dominance has flattened German football's competitive balance for over a decade.

teams.name: Borussia Dortmund
teams.drivers: Your club. Yellow Wall, Ruhr Valley working-class roots, 50+1 fan ownership.

teams.name: Borussia Mönchengladbach
teams.drivers: The old "Fohlenelf," well-supported and 50+1 owned, but doesn't carry the same underdog mythology as the clubs above it.

teams.name: Eintracht Frankfurt
teams.drivers: A real, loud ultras scene and a 2022 Europa League win that's pulled the club further into the commercial spotlight since.

teams.name: FC Augsburg
teams.drivers: Unpretentious Bavarian club, modest scale, no real corporate baggage.

teams.name: Hamburger SV
teams.drivers: The only ever-present club until 2018's relegation, genuine history, but years of boardroom chaos have eroded the identity.

teams.name: Mainz 05
teams.drivers: Modest budget, homegrown ethos, the club that gave Klopp his start and never lost the plot chasing money.

teams.name: RB Leipzig
teams.drivers: Built by Red Bull to route around the 50+1 rule via a shell membership scheme, boycotted by supporter groups across the league. The clearest sportswashing-adjacent case in German football, same category as PSG or Man City on your other tables.

teams.name: SC Freiburg
teams.drivers: The Streich-era model: sustainable, homegrown, unglamorous, and genuinely community-run in the Black Forest.

teams.name: SC Paderborn
teams.drivers: Same story as Elversberg: small, newly promoted, honest but unproven at this level.

teams.name: SV Elversberg
teams.drivers: Newly promoted, grassroots Saarland roots, too new at this level to have built a deeper reputation yet.

teams.name: Schalke 04
teams.drivers: Gelsenkirchen mining heritage runs deep, one of Germany's largest member bases, currently paying for years of financial mismanagement but the culture is real.

teams.name: TSG Hoffenheim
teams.drivers: Bankrolled almost entirely by Dietmar Hopp's software fortune, widely treated across German football as the artificial-rise club, the target of some of the league's most pointed fan protests.

teams.name: Union Berlin
teams.drivers: Fans literally built terraces with their own hands to keep the stadium alive, refused a shirt sponsor for years, East Berlin working-class identity that never chased polish.

teams.name: VfB Stuttgart
teams.drivers: Big traditional support, but Mercedes-Benz's ownership stake and sponsorship ties give it a corporate edge the smaller clubs above don't have.

teams.name: Werder Bremen
teams.drivers: Historic Weserstadion, genuine Bundesliga tradition, working-class North German identity.

bl.tv: Fandango, free (marquee games on USA Network)

teams.name: Angel City FC
teams.drivers: Celebrity-founded brand club with huge crowds, now controlled by the Iger family. Heavy on marketing, light on roots.

teams.name: Bay FC
teams.drivers: Founded in 2024 with private-equity money (Sixth Street) as majority owner.

teams.name: Boston Legacy
teams.drivers: Brings top-flight women's football back to Boston, where the founding Breakers folded in 2018. New investor-owned club.

teams.name: Chicago Stars
teams.drivers: Founding club (the Red Stars) that endured years of neglect under a failed owner and still plays in a small college stadium.

teams.name: Denver Summit
teams.drivers: Brand-new 2026 club that drew 63,004 to Mile High in its first season.

teams.name: Gotham FC
teams.drivers: Founding club (Sky Blue FC) that spent a decade in a college stadium in Piscataway before the Harrison move and two titles.

teams.name: Houston Dash
teams.drivers: Early expansion side (2014) run alongside the Dynamo, loyal but small following.

teams.name: Kansas City Current
teams.drivers: Built CPKC Stadium, the first stadium made for a women's team, and fills it every week. Wealthy owners, but money spent on the women's game itself.

teams.name: North Carolina Courage
teams.drivers: Heir to the Western New York Flash, a founding club, and the dominant side of the late 2010s. Docked for the 2017 relocation.

teams.name: Orlando Pride
teams.drivers: Run as the women's arm of MLS Orlando City, a corporate sibling rather than a standalone club.

teams.name: Portland Thorns
teams.drivers: Founding 2013 club and the league's supporter-culture benchmark: the Rose City Riveters and the biggest regular crowds. New ownership after the 2022 abuse scandal forced the old owner out.

teams.name: Racing Louisville
teams.drivers: Community-rooted Kentucky club sharing Lynn Family Stadium with Louisville City. Modest budget, local ownership.

teams.name: San Diego Wave
teams.drivers: Big crowds since 2022, sold to a private-equity firm in 2024.

teams.name: Seattle Reign
teams.drivers: Founding club with a real supporter base, but years as OL Reign under the Lyon multi-club group and a revolving door of names and stadiums.

teams.name: Utah Royals
teams.drivers: Refounded in 2024 by the Real Salt Lake group after the first Royals were moved to Kansas City.

teams.name: Washington Spirit
teams.drivers: Founding club with the Spirit Squadron and big Audi Field crowds. Docked for owner Michele Kang's multi-club group with Lyon and London City.
